name: Cameco
description: Cameco mines uranium in northern Saskatchewan (Cigar Lake and McArthur River/Key Lake, plus 50% of Inkai in Kazakhstan), converts it into fuel-ready forms in its fuel services segment, and owns 49% of Westinghouse, one of the world's largest nuclear reactor and services companies (51% is Brookfield's). Uranium is sold to utilities mostly under long-term contracts (average realized price US$62.11 a pound in 2025, against an average spot price of US$73.54 and a long-term price of US$81.96), so revenue lags the spot market. Westinghouse is not consolidated: Cameco books its 49% share of earnings, and that share is now a big part of profit (C$780 million of adjusted EBITDA in 2025, against C$483 million in 2024, out of C$1,929 million total). Revenue was C$3,482 million in 2025 (+11%), net earnings C$590 million and adjusted net earnings C$627 million. It pays an annual dividend of C$0.24 per share.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge (uranium miners sit here, alongside coal); not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code 1090 (Miscellaneous Metal Ores). It is really a nuclear-fuel-cycle company that also owns 49% of a reactor maker, which the coal-and-fuels box hides.

businessLines.name: Uranium
businessLines.shareBasis: 2,874 of 3,482 million consolidated revenue (Uranium 2,874 + Fuel services 562 = 3,436; the remaining 46 million is other/eliminations, derived)
businessLines.how: Sells uranium concentrate (U3O8) to utilities under long-term contracts that blend fixed and market-linked prices, so revenue follows volumes delivered and prices set when contracts were signed rather than today's spot price.
businessLines.description: Mining and milling at McArthur River/Key Lake and Cigar Lake in the Athabasca Basin, a 50% share of JV Inkai (Kazakhstan, equity accounted, bought back as purchases), and purchases and trading of uranium.

revenue.note: 2024: 2,677 (+7%); sales volume 33.0 million lb (33.6 in 2024); average realized price C$87.00/lb, US$62.11/lb

businessLines.name: Fuel services
businessLines.how: Fees per kilogram converted or fabricated under multi-year utility contracts; the contract mix is steadier than uranium.
businessLines.description: Refining and conversion of uranium into UF6, UO2 and UO3 and fuel fabrication.

businessLines.name: Westinghouse (49% equity interest; Brookfield owns 51%)
businessLines.how: Long-term contracts for outage services, fuel and components across the installed base of reactors, plus multi-year new-build project revenue (for example two reactors at Dukovany, Czech Republic, led by Korea Hydro and Nuclear Power).
businessLines.description: Nuclear reactor technology maker (AP1000) and provider of fuel, servicing, parts and new-build projects to utilities worldwide; 2025 total revenue was US$5.0 billion (100% basis). Cameco's share is booked as equity earnings, not revenue.
